newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu flat, market digesting c.bank moves.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu flat, market digesting c.bank moves.

text.p: Romania's leu ended steady on Thursday at 5,950/980 to the dollar on an interbank market hit by hard currency shortages, with traders digesting a jump in the central bank's one-week refinancing rate.
"We expected a further tightening in the central bank's monetary policy but the upswing by 10 points was more than we thought," said one trader.

The central bank on Thursday pushed on with its drive to temper a surge in inflation and rebuild confidence in the leu by lifting the one-week rate to 80 percent from 70 and cutting refinancing funds to 550 billion lei from 750 billion.
One-week rates hovered near 67 percent in a cash-starved money market as banks rushed to meet their mandatory reserves at the end of the month.
"Prices will go up tomorrow as the market will react to the rise in the refinancing rate," said one trader.
Cross quotes of other currencies rebounded Thursday offering a leu-dollar price of 6,050 against 6,500 in the past few days.

Forex traders have used cross trading in other currencies since last March, when the market was restricted to four dealer banks by the former ruling leftists to keep the leu overvalued against the dollar ahead of elections.

Operators said the narrowing of direct rates and cross rates, which iron out months-old distortions on the market, might reduce liquidity for a while. But it would also offer support to the leu, which has lost some 45 percent against the dollar since January 1.
Leu-dollar retail rates lingered at about 6,000/200.
The market awaited also details of the reform package which Romania's new centrist coalition government was negotiating with international lenders.

Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea was holding a news confrence late on Thursday to give the first details of pledges made in exchange for renewed funds from the International Monetary Fund, which suspended credits to Romania last year.
